blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — BiDil adjunctive heart-failure indication
stem: A self-identified Black client with chronic heart failure is prescribed isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine (BiDil) in addition to standard therapy. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: BiDil is labeled as adjunct therapy to standard heart-failure treatment to improve survival, delay heart-failure hospitalization, and improve patient-reported functional status.
options.B: BiDil is used mainly for blood-pressure reduction in this setting and does not have a labeled heart-failure indication involving survival, hospitalization, or functional status.
options.C: BiDil replaces the client's other standard heart-failure medications once it is started because the combination is intended to function as complete stand-alone therapy.
options.D: BiDil works through beta-receptor blockade by hydralazine and calcium-channel blockade by isosorbide dinitrate, which is the basis of its heart-failure benefit.

rationale: Current BiDil labeling states that the isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine combination is indicated as adjunct therapy to standard therapy in self-identified Black patients with heart failure to improve survival, prolong time to hospitalization for heart failure, and improve patient-reported functional status. Therefore A is correct. B ignores the labeled heart-failure outcomes, C incorrectly substitutes the combination for standard therapy, and D assigns mechanisms the components do not have; the label describes isosorbide dinitrate as a nitrate vasodilator and hydralazine as an arteriolar vasodilator.
educational_objective: Recognize the FDA-labeled role of isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine as adjunct heart-failure therapy in self-identified Black patients and distinguish it from replacement therapy or unrelated pharmacologic mechanisms.
source_document_title: BIDIL (isosorbide dinitrate and hydralazine hydrochloride) — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: DailyMed updated November 30, 2025; prescribing information revised November 2025; current label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §1.1 Treatment of Heart Failure in Self-identified Black Patients: BiDil is indicated as adjunct to standard therapy to improve survival, prolong time to heart-failure hospitalization, and improve patient-reported functional status. Highlights identify isosorbide dinitrate as a nitrate vasodilator and hydralazine as an arteriolar vasodilator.
source_claim_supported: BiDil is FDA-labeled as adjunctive standard heart-failure therapy in self-identified Black patients to improve survival, delay heart-failure hospitalization, and improve patient-reported functional status.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication appropriateness, educate clients, and understand expected medication actions/outcomes.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete heart-failure indication/mechanism statements of comparable length.
Preserved all three labeled adjunctive outcomes without leaving the correct answer uniquely long.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current November 2025 BiDil label. Options are tightly length-matched and no second defensible explanation remains.
